The X server uses hardware optimized sprites for the cursor where avaiable. Cursor fonts are just bitmaps. If you want to change the way in which cursors are handled, you'd have to re-write that part of X (Xorg, but who knows it that won't have been replaced with Wayland in ten years).

It might seem useful to adjust the colour and brightness of the cursor to contrast with the background, but that introduces the problem of how to deal with greys (colours where the inverse has the same brightness). The Windows cursor here is either black or white, incapable of colour and nuance, and thus by-passes the problem, but you can use high contrast cursor fonts in X as well.

The Windows cursor bitmaps are available as cursor font, but the I-beam won't change colour like it does here. You could use dithering (alternating black and white pixels) to make it visible against any background.

I, personally, don't do any formal stretching. My philosophy behind this is that I already practice the movements that I seek to excel at, and that the practice thereof is enough for all of the functional flexibility I need to do so. Thus, any more flexibility I might gain from static stretching wouldn't do me any good.

Note that I do almost entirely bodyweight movements that are quite a bit more flexibility intensive than weightlifting movements, so this approach has left me more than flexible enough for anything I'd ever need to do in daily life. If you did this with squats, bench, and deadlifts, there's a good chance you'd eventually get so tight that it would begin to interfere with daily tasks. So, YMMV.

Another reason bodyweight rules, though.

It's a really bad idea to stretch when weight training. Martial arts is one of the only sports stretching is actually useful for. Other than gymnastics, dancing, and martial arts, people really SHOULDN'T be stretching.

That and people at gyms are often there to just use the equipment and do things they can't do at home. They can stretch at home, no need to crowd up the gym for it.

Lastly, the great majority (80%+) people at a gym, including trainers, have no clue what they're doing in regards to proper form or mechanics. They'd rather spend all their time and money on things that have literally zero value (like protein supplements) it's no surprise that stretching doesn't make the list.

TLDR: Stretching isn't cool so people don't do it, but they don't really need to anyways.

There are arguments on both sides on whether or not static stretching is beneficial, and possibly even harmful. I do a light warmup and low weight/ no weight "stretching", I don't do any traditional static stretching.
